id: BACK TO EVERLY - FUNDRAISER GIG-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
name: BACK TO EVERLY - FUNDRAISER GIG
long_description:
Come support student filmmaking and student bands at Valhalla!
Tickets here
Come along for a night of awesome music to support our short film Back to Everly! Headlined by Cattails, this night is going to be a ride - so strap in and get ready!
Bands playing (in order of appearance)
Boyband - Boyband hits you where it hurts, soothes you where it matters most and hopes to get the people moving. Bringing a blend of pop, neo-soul and alternative music, boyband is ready to get the night started!
Maddeypuppets - Maddeypuppets bring a mix of acoustic soul rock!
Dystonia - Alternative metal band ready to get you pumping!
Cattails - A poprock band based in Wellington, Cattails are guaranteed to keep you boogying all night long!
What are we fundraising for?
Back to Everly is a short psychological drama-thriller set in a pastel, idealized world inspired by 1950s aesthetics. Society is built around a daily pill called Everly, which is believed to be essential for survival. Its use is completely normalized and reinforced through constant propaganda embedded in television, advertisements, and music, shaping a world where no one ever questions its necessity.
This film explores themes of conformity, control, and conditioned belief systems. At its core, Back to Everly asks how easily people accept systems of “truth” without questioning their origin or purpose.
We are raising money for:
Art Department - $2000 of our budget will go towards costuming, props, hair and makeup, and set design. 
Payment - We want to give back and express our appreciation to our talented cast. 
Food - We want to accommodate and ensure everyone on our set is fed and looked after, as the crew is giving us their time for free
Transport - Though we aren't paying our crew, transportation to and from set is expensive. Funds will go towards van hire and gas payments. 
Come along and support this awesome cause!

name: MORTIIS AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON
long_description:
Valhalla Touring are proud to present from the Cold Dark Depths of Norway MORTIIS, with special guest Windswept.
MORTIIS needs no introduction to the Metal world, famous for being the bass player in early EMPEROR, Mortiis has since carved a long and respected career in the Dark Dungeon Synth world for the last 3 + decades. Mortiis has performed in Australia before as a solo one man show, but this time Aotearoa will be treated to something very special... he will be bringing his band with him for the very first time, performing songs from The Smell Of Rain album and other volumes of Dystopian Despair. This is a first and not to be missed.
Check out new MORTIIS - Ghosts Of Europa https://youtu.be/PQcBobUAwsE
Wellingtons very own black metal powerhouse Windswept, are locked in to bring their unholy chaos to the stage as the official support on both shows. Their debut album Howling in Baptismal Filth recently released on US label Northern Void Records has made a big impact, debuting on the official Aoteoroa music charts
Check out the video for Cenote https://youtu.be/kKjBtlRwxkMsi=p-OAFUeew7eSOr7Y

name: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026
long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.
Tickets here

id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON
long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.
It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.
Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”
This event is at Meow
Tickets here

name: GREAT SOUNDS GREAT 2026
long_description:
Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.
Tickets here
Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.
Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.
Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.
Limited tickets, including for The Night Before, on sale now from eyegum.co.nz/great-sounds-great
Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.
Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.
Lineup: Amamelia, Beastwars, Bic Runga, Bri Louise, Chris Tse, Crook, Cruelly, Dani Yourukova, Deathro (JPN), Dream Chambers, Fazed on a Pony, Groove Council, Hemi Hemingway, Hihi & The Stitchbirds, Hunter Jackson, In Good Company, Jackson McCarthy, JELL, Ludus b2b Rizzo, MĀ, Mauri Aura, mHz, Mokotron, More Blue Noise, Naakz & Babyzoot, Office Dog, Pearly*, Pitch Black, Savage (DJ Set), Savagehine, Sheeps, Silicon, So So Modern, Soft Bait, Tamatha Paul, The Sour, The Spectre Collective: Live-Scored Cinema, Tūi Band, Unsanitary Napkin.
